chunks: 2148 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And whoever enters it shall be secure."

He said: "Whoever heads for this House while knowing that it is the House which Allah has commanded, and knows us, the Ahl al-Bayt, with the true recognition of us, shall be secure in this world and the Hereafter.

And it has been narrated: "Whoever commits an offense and then seeks refuge in the Haram, the hadd is not carried out upon him, and he is neither fed, nor given drink, nor given water, nor sheltered, until he leaves the Haram, whereupon the hadd is carried out upon him. But if he commits within the Haram that which necessitates the hadd, he is seized for it within the Haram, because he did not regard the Haram as having sanctity."

key_terms.آمِنًا: secure, safe in worldly and ultimate terms
key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the family of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم whose recognition is required here
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary surrounding the House
key_terms.حَقَّ مَعْرِفَتِنَا: true and proper recognition of their rank and authority

ai.seo_question: What does "And whoever enters it shall be secure" mean in Shia hadith, and what are the legal rulings for seeking refuge in the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse "And whoever enters it shall be secure" by linking the security of the Sacred House to both outward pilgrimage and true recognition of Ahl al-Bayt. It also states a legal ruling concerning one who seeks refuge in the Haram after a crime, while preserving the sanctity of the Haram and distinguishing between crimes committed outside it and within it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2148 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said regarding the words of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic,
"And whoever enters it shall be secure" (Surah Aal-e-Imran 3:97)

: "Whoever visits this House knowing that it is the House that Allah (swt) has commanded and recognizes our right, the Ahlulbayt, with true recognition, shall be secure in this world and the Hereafter."

It has also been narrated: "Whoever commits a crime and then seeks refuge in the Haram will not have the prescribed punishment (Hadd) carried out against them. However, they will neither be given food nor drink nor shelter until they leave the Haram, at which point the Hadd will be carried out. If someone commits a crime within the Haram that requires Hadd, they will be taken within the Haram itself because they have shown no regard for its sanctity."
